answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by charging every new identity a refundable stake that is slashed when its work is judged fake. Like a juniper that grows slowly and cannot be cloned overnight, reputation must be earned through attested tasks over time, so an attacker who spins up a thousand fresh accounts at dawn pays a thousand stakes and still has no history to spend. The real pulse of the network - peer attestations tied to staked work - then costs more to fake than any honest participant pays to join.
